Can Devlegate checkpoint these edits and run mandatory hosted CI, including the complete suite, coverage, and lint, at that exact successor checkpoint?
worker_claim.report: All five reviewed failures passed (5.29 s). Both touched modules passed (186 tests), as did 73 focused candidate/reconciliation/recovery tests, 10 shared active/REWORK replay checks, and all four real-service reconciliation topology variants on an isolated rerun. Lint and git diff --check passed. Broader supplemental batches exceeded the local tool deadline and are not counted as passing. No production edits or new production defect established. Relative to TASK-199's admitted base (6d4388c), tracked Python LOC changed from 42,869 to 42,329 in src and 58,087 to 57,415 in tests; collection changed from 2,758 to 2,737 cases. The same five logical regression nodes took 8.68 s on the base and 5.29 s on the successor, with different fixture work and run conditions. The cumulative refactor replaces reconciliation_transactions.py and the separate rework_transfer.py, removing old in-place rebase, local/remote pending rewrite, native abort/continue, and implementation-only mock/fault tests. Retained coverage includes Git lineage/authorization, immutable evidence, conflict confirmation, replay after candidate/install/publication effects, authority refusals, same-base replay, zero-delta retry, and distinct continuation semantics.
worker_claim.summary: Reconciliation classification tests now use real Git observations of unchanged and advanced product generations, including a published execution ref. The topology tests import the relocated helper directly and retain their Git assertions.
